correctness.rationale: For a generator z of the center, the identity with a central second argument gives B(gz^j)=B(g)B(z)^j. With first argument z, put [B(z),h]=z^k; reduction modulo the center forces k times the quotient class of B(z) to vanish. If that class is nonzero, nondegeneracy gives an h with k nonzero, impossible over the prime field. After preservation of the center, the quotient map A is additive and hence linear. The central coordinate equation has symmetric left side Q(v+w)-Q(v)-Q(w); antisymmetrizing gives (1), and its symmetric part is the polarization of -(c/2)ω(Av,v). The remaining term is additive, hence precisely an arbitrary linear functional; reversing verifies sufficiency. In the c=0 and -1 strata the counted map A or I+A has isotropic image. At stage i of an ordered isotropic frame the new vector lies in an orthogonal space of dimension 2m-i but outside the current i-plane. Dividing the resulting product by the ordered basis count and multiplying by the number of surjections and by p^(2m) gives (2), including rank zero. The generic chart is reversible only where I+A is invertible, as stated. The supplemental verifier is not an exhaustive search of arbitrary set maps or a proof for all p,m and was not executed.
